# tcpshield_sentry_tunnel (Data Source)

Reads a single Sentry tunnel, including its bandwidth counters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "tcpshield_sentry_tunnel" "game" {
  id = 42
}

output "monthly_bytes" {
  value = data.tcpshield_sentry_tunnel.game.month_bandwidth_usage
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (Number) Numeric tunnel id.

### Read-Only

- `bind_port` (Number) Port the tunnel binds on TCPShield's side.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `cumulative_bandwidth_usage` (Number) Total bandwidth used in bytes.
- `current_bandwidth_usage` (Number) Current bandwidth usage in bytes.
- `egress` (Number) Egress in bytes.
- `endpoint_peer` (String) Public address of the origin's WireGuard peer.
- `endpoint_private_key` (String, Sensitive) WireGuard private key generated for the origin's endpoint.
- `endpoint_public_key` (String) WireGuard public key of the origin's endpoint.
- `ingress` (Number) Ingress in bytes.
- `location` (String) Location key.
- `month_bandwidth_usage` (Number) Bandwidth used this month in bytes.
- `name` (String) Tunnel name.
- `tunnel_addresses` (Attributes List) Addresses allocated to the tunnel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tunnel_addresses))

<a id="nestedatt--tunnel_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tunnel_addresses`

Read-Only:

- `ip_address_private` (String) Private tunnel IP on TCPShield's side.
- `ip_address_public` (String) Public IP clients connect to.
- `location` (String) Location of the address.
- `peer_ip_address_private` (String) Private tunnel IP of the origin.
